npcs.name: Guard Tobin
lines: The North Gate. The Old Road runs up past the Fields — keep to it after dark.
Goblins have been at the Fields' wall again. The captain wants them seen to.

npcs.name: Guard Fenn
lines: Move along, friend. Nothing gets past this gate that we don't see.
Rats in the old barn, hens at Wenna's, cows in the pasture. Start small.

npcs.name: Guard Isla
lines: The Quarry Gate. The quarry is down the lane to the west — every ore in the Vale, they say.
The arena's past the gate, south-east. Quiet now; it won't be for long.

npcs.name: Guard Rowe
lines: The Hill Gate. The hill road climbs to Greyfell — iron and trolls, mostly trolls.
The air altar is just past the gate, north of the road. Mages come and go all day.

npcs.name: Guard Ash
lines: The Wood Gate. The wood lane runs to the Thornwood. Spiders. Big ones.
Blank stone lies pale in the rocks by the lane, if you've a pick — the stuff runes are carved from.

npcs.name: Guard Merrow
lines: All quiet in the market.
If you find trouble outside the walls, run for a gate. We'll keep the rest out.

npcs.name: Guard Cole
lines: Walking the street, as ever.
The bank's on the market, east side. Keep your coin there, not in your boots.

npcs.name: Captain Hale
lines: I keep Ashbrook's walls from this tower — Hale's Tower, the town calls it, after my grandfather. My guards keep the gates; I keep the guards.
Steel at your side and food in your bag — that's the whole of the advice I give.

npcs.name: Banker Odo
lines: Welcome to the bank of Ashbrook. What you leave with me is safe — from thieves, from fire, and from your own bad luck.

npcs.name: Merrit
lines: Tools for every trade — axes and picks in bronze, iron and steel, nets, rods, cages, snares, needles. Food's at the larder across the market, weapons at the armoury next door. I'll buy whatever you don't need.
A better axe bites faster, and a better pick too — if your arm can use it: iron at ten, steel at twenty.

npcs.name: Hobb
lines: Blades and armour, made at the smithy and the craft workshop: bronze and leather to start, iron at ten, steel at twenty. Plate turns a blade but dulls a spell. Buy, then try.

npcs.name: Ama
lines: Bows, arrows, and everything to make your own — shafts, feathers, tips; fifteen of each for fifteen arrows. The yew longbow's for a steady hand at thirty. The fletcher's bench is down on Craft Lane.

npcs.name: Sefa
lines: Vials, herbs and a few brews of my own. The alchemist's table is on Craft Lane if you'd rather mix your own — you brew for the craft, mind, not the coin.

npcs.name: Bess
lines: Food for the road, cooked and raw. The bakehouse range on Craft Lane is free to use.
Flour? Knead it and bake it at the bakehouse range, or any good fire — a loaf for every sack. I sell a sack, if Garrow's wheel has turned.

npcs.name: Ysolde
lines: Runes for every spell you can cast here — air, water, fire, focus and wild — staffs to cast them through, and a robe that suits the work.
Blank stone lies by the wood lane if you'd rather carve your own at the altars; an altar carves the whole bag at once.
Oath runes, too, for Homeward: they carry you back to the market cross from anywhere in the Vale.

npcs.name: Orla
lines: The Hearth's fire is always lit, and the yard fire behind is yours to cook on. Travellers sleep here; their horses next door.

npcs.name: Brannoc
lines: Furnace to smelt, anvil to shape. Bring me ore and I'll show you both.
Bring me a tool, a couple of bars and the coin, and I'll temper it fine — a keener edge, a better balance. You'll feel the difference by the tenth log.

npcs.name: Brother Aldous
lines: The church's altar restores the spirit. Pray there whenever your blessings run thin.

npcs.name: Master Edda
lines: The guildhall keeps every guild's records. Every skill grows by doing — cut, mine, fish, fight, and come tell me how far you've come.
Open your skills and you'll see the Hall's records too.

npcs.name: Scholar Wren
lines: The library will hold all the Vale's lore. One day you'll research here — new recipes, new spells, the beasts' weaknesses.
Books are slow. Slower than you'd like. Faster than forgetting.

npcs.name: Grimwald
lines: Grimwald. I keep the slayer book: what needs killing, where, and how many. Take a task, finish it, come back. Every fifth one done in a row, the purse is heavier.
Skip a task if you must — it costs you coin, not your streak. The Vale is full of things that want thinning.

npcs.name: Marta
lines: The arena. Beasts from every corner of the Vale, and coin for whoever's standing at the end. Pay the fee, step onto the sand. My purse for each beast is paid once a day.
Beat all five in a row — goblin, wolf, boar, troll, wyvern — and the cup is yours, with the champion's purse. Fall, and the run starts again.
Fall out there and my people drag you off — you lose the fee and your pride, nothing else.

npcs.name: Tamsin
lines: Hides make leather, leather makes armour. The workbench is behind me.

npcs.name: Joss
lines: Shrimp in the mill pond, herring in the brook. Bring a net.

npcs.name: Garrow the miller
lines: The wheel grinds for the whole Vale when it turns. Dunn carts the flour to Bess's bakehouse.
Flour, planks and iron — a mill eats all three.

npcs.name: Pell
lines: Market day, every day. Whatever you need, someone on this square sells it.
They say the Old Quarry goes deeper than anyone's dug.

npcs.name: Wenna
lines: Mind the hens, they peck. And mind the rats at the old barn — they're into my feed again.

npcs.name: Ailith
lines: New to the Vale? I show newcomers the ropes: a tree, a hen, a rock. Three small jobs and you'll know the land — whatever kit you came with, there's an axe and a pick in your bag.
Every skill levels by doing it. The panel at the top shows them tick up.

npcs.name: Ranger Corwin
lines: The Thornwood starts here. Wolves on the moor, boars in the deep, and bandits camped past the goblins.
Walk soft and keep a hen in your bag. The wood doesn't care how brave you are.

npcs.name: Foreman Dunstan
lines: Greyfell's richest seams — iron, coal, and steel-stone if your arm's good enough.
The trolls' cave is at the end of the road east. Don't go knocking.

npcs.name: Marl
lines: Shrimp and herring, fresh this morning. Bess at the larder has the cooked ones.

npcs.name: Idony
lines: Wool from the hill flocks, dyed in the town. The tanner does the leather; I do the cloth.
Tired of your colours? My vats will take any cloth or leather you wear — blue, green, wine, ochre, black. A visit's two hundred.

npcs.name: Tamsel the barber
lines: Sit down, sit down. A trim, a new colour, something with a bit of style? A hundred and fifty, and you'll walk out a new face.
Half the Vale's heads have been in my chair. The other half should be.

npcs.name: Wat
lines: Pots, jugs and crocks. Drop one and it's yours.

npcs.name: Agnes
lines: They read the charter from the cross, every fair day.
The church bell carries to the mill when the wind's from the south.

npcs.name: Hob
lines: Well water's sweet. The fountain's for the horses.
Hale's Tower keeps the key to the gates. Nobody's out after the bell.

npcs.name: Mabb
lines: North Lane. The church is at the east end, the tower at the west.

npcs.name: Rab
lines: Craft Lane: the tanner, the fletcher, the alchemist and the bakehouse. Smell the bread? That's the east end.

npcs.name: Nell
lines: The Wood Gate's at the end of this street. Past it, the lane to the Thornwood.

npcs.name: Piers
lines: Brannoc's smithy is in the yard there. You'll hear it before you see it.

npcs.name: Edith
lines: The Hearth inn, on the left before the gate. Orla keeps a good fire.

npcs.name: Col
lines: Wenna's hens are outside the North Gate. Her rats are at the old barn past them.

npcs.name: Gammer Tibb
lines: I've sat on this market seventy years. It was grass when I was a girl.

npcs.name: Dunn the carter
lines: Gate to gate and back, all day. Mind the cart.
Flour from the mill, iron from the quarry, hides to the tanner. Everything in Ashbrook comes through this road.

npcs.name: Old Hesper
lines: The road ends at the cross a little south. Nothing past it but grass and the sky, and that suits me.
Pray at the shrine at the cross if you're going on. It's the last one.

npcs.name: Hew the woodcutter
lines: The old forest: oak and ash at the edge, pines up the slope, yews at the heart — nothing cuts a yew under sixty. The sawmill makes planks of any log.
There's a glade under the oldest yew, west along the track. Folk pray there. Wolves den on the way; mind them.
Nests in the high canopies, mushroom rings on the floor, and a hunter's hide if you want to watch the deer.

npcs.name: Wick the lamplighter
lines: Dusk's my hour. Every lamp from the Quarry Gate to the North Gate, then the street — and the bell lights the rest.
Mind the pole. Oil on it.

npcs.name: Teodor the merchant
lines: Teodor, merchant of the King's Road — the south cross to the North Gate and back, every day the weather lets me. Rare stock, road prices.
North today, to the gate, if the axle holds. When the light goes I camp at the Fields' fire; find me there.

npcs.name: Ned the carter
lines: Axle's gone — snapped clean on that rut. Two pine logs and I could splint it and be off. I'd pay.
If you've two logs on you, I'd be glad of them.

npcs.name: Tam
lines: I went after a rabbit and the road turned and... can you take me back to the gate? Please?
Are we nearly there?

npcs.name: Pim the pedlar
lines: Odds and ends, cheap as you like — I'd sooner sell it than carry it another mile.
